sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Sliding window is a **two-pointer** technique for problems on **contiguous subranges** of arrays or strings. The window is bounded by left and right and adjusts dynamically with the condition.
items: right keeps **expanding**, pulling new elements into the window
When the window stops satisfying the condition, left **shrinks** it until the condition holds again
The window may be **fixed-size** or **dynamically sized** by the condition
Only the state inside the window (sum, character counts, etc.) is maintained, never recomputed from scratch

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Since left and right only move forward, each element enters and leaves the window at most once.
items: **Space complexity**: usually [[success|O(1)]]; with character counts it is [[warning|O(k)]], k being the number of distinct characters
The key is updating state **incrementally** in O(1) as elements enter and leave

sections.heading: When to Use It
sections.content: The signals for a sliding window are "contiguous" and "monotonicity".
items: **Contiguous subarray / substring**: e.g. longest substring without repeats, maximum sum of length K
**Monotonicity**: growing the window makes the condition harder (or easier) to meet, so you know when to shrink
**Limit**: with negative numbers and a "sum at least target" condition, monotonicity fails — use prefix sums or similar
